documents.abstract: With the widespread adoption of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), the need for effective ADAS driver training increases. However, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of ADAS education remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of an ADAS driver training program across four European countries. The training included classroom-based theoretical instruction and practical hands-on experience on test-tracks and open-roads. 166 participants completed a questionnaire measuring their knowledge, attitudes, and behavioral intentions towards ADAS pre- and post-training. Overall knowledge of system purpose, handling and limitations improved significantly with the training. However, some misunderstandings remained, and in some cases, misconceptions from before the training were not corrected. Perceived safety and trust remained unchanged while willingness to use ADAS systems, and the perceived ease of use and usefulness of ADAS increased. Future training should not only provide information for trainees but also identify misconceptions they may hold. Follow-up or feedback sessions are recommended to address potential misunderstandings.

documents.abstract: Chronic or recurrent pain significantly impairs quality of life, and conventional pharmacological treatments often produce side effects, motivating the search for non-pharmacological alternatives. This study introduces a novel paradigm — E-Tactile Tactile Flow (E-Tactile Flow)—which integrates electrotactile stimulation with attentional engagement and flow-related task design. Inspired by a bidirectional attention mechanism, the paradigm designed goal-directed task mode and stimulus-driven task mode to examine the role of cognitive engagement in pain modulation. A preliminary study validated the feasibility and safety parameters of an 8×8 electrotactile system. In Experiment 1 (n = 42), both attention modes effectively reduced pain perception, with the goal-directed task mode showing significantly stronger modulation of several physiological measures and a marginal trend toward lower subjective pain ratings than the stimulus-driven task mode. Building on this, Experiment 2 introduced adaptive difficulty modulation to better align task challenge with participant performance. Results showed that dynamic task adjustment significantly enhanced attentional engagement and reduced pain ratings. Overall, this study provides initial empirical support for an electrotactile interaction paradigm for non-pharmacological pain modulation.

EcoPro-LSTM is version 0 of Ecosystem Process Modelling using a Long Short-Term Memory Approach. The model uses a Multi-Task Multi-Timescale Long Short-Term Memory (MT-LSTM) modelling framework. EcoPro-LSTM was developed by Mitra Cattry et al. as part of the research “EcoPro-LSTM v0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments,” accepted for publication in Machine Learning: Earth (2026). The work was financially supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation, Award #P500PN_206603, and the National Science Foundation (NSF) Science and Technology Center (STC) Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP), Award #2019625-STC. The model predicts environmental variables including gross primary productivity (carbon uptake), ecosystem respiration, evapotranspiration, and surface soil moisture across multiple timescales using a single LSTM architecture, as described in the accompanying tutorial. Integrated gradients are used to enhance model interpretability by identifying the influence of climatic drivers such as precipitation. For questions, issues, or further assistance with the code, please contact Mitra Cattry at mitra.cattry@gmail.com. (2026). EcoPro-LSTM v0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments.Machine Learning: Earth. Accepted. KG_climate.zip — Köppen–Geiger climate classifications and associated code used to identify Mediterranean and semi-arid FLUXNET2015 sites. ablation_processed_files.zip — Processed ablation results, including site-level MAE across GPP thresholds on the test sets for all model configurations, together with the Python code used to plot the results.

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence edge computing, and autonomous systems is transforming the nature of modern warfare. Traditional defense operations, which relied heavily on centralized command structures and human decision-making, are increasingly being augmented by intelligent systems capable of sensing, analyzing, and responding to dynamic battlefield conditions in real time. Among these technologies, Edge AI has emerged as a critical enabler of smart warfare by allowing data processing and AI inference to occur directly on deployed platforms rather than relying on distant cloud infrastructures. This chapter explores the role of Edge AI in defense operations, with particular emphasis on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), autonomous surveillance systems and intelligent reconnaissance platforms. It further examines the use of Edge AI for applications such as target recognition, battlefield situational awareness, autonomous navigation, mission execution, and decentralized decision-making.

Introduction This study examines the pedagogical integration of educommunication and artificial intelligence (AI) and its association with self-reported professional competencies among university prosumers-students who simultaneously consume, produce, and share academic content through digital platforms. Methods A non-experimental, cross-sectional quantitative design with descriptive-correlational and structural purposes was employed. Data were collected using a psychometrically validated 26-item Likert-scale questionnaire (plus six open-response items) administered to a convenience sample of 547 university students enrolled at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Ecuador. The instrument assessed five dimensions: (1) AI-mediated learning processes, (2) educommunication and expression, (3) knowledge prosumption, (4) perceived professional competencies, and (5) ethics and critical AI use. Psychometric validation confirmed excellent reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.91; McDonald's ω = 0.93). Exploratory factor analysis supported the five-factor structure (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.91; Bartlett's test p < 0.001; variance explained = 61.4%). Confirmatory factor analysis indicated a satisfactory model fit (comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.96; Tucker-Lewis index [TLI] = 0.95; root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.052; standardized root mean square residual [SRMR] = 0.061). A single-factor test yielded a first unrotated factor accounting for 28.3% of the variance, below the 50% threshold, offering a preliminary indication against a single dominant method factor, although this test alone does not rule out common method bias (see Section 3.3). Results Structural equation modeling revealed significant direct paths from AI-mediated learning to perceived professional competencies ( β = 0.58, p < 0.001) and from educommunication to knowledge prosumption ( β = 0.51, p < 0.001), with knowledge prosumption partially mediating the educommunication-competency association ( β _indirect = 0.21; R² = 0.74 for D3; R² = 0.78 for D4), and ethics and critical AI use functioning as a significant moderator of the AI learning-competency path (interaction β = 0.34, p < 0.001). Given the cross-sectional, self-report design, these results are interpreted as structural associations rather than causal effects. Discussion Findings indicate that AI integration within educommunicative frameworks is positively associated with autonomous learning, creativity, and digital communication skills. However, risks associated with technological over-reliance and epistemic dependency were also identified in the qualitative data. These findings constitute structurally validated evidence that pedagogical AI integration, framed within educommunicative approaches, is associated with the perceived development of critical, collaborative, and innovative professional competencies in higher education.

Background: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) affect most dental hygienists.While advances in design can reduce the biomechanical strain associated with instrumentation, the literature offers little guidance on rest-break parameters, or on how instrument design may modify those requirements.Goal was to map the effect of rigid vs adaptive handle design on fatigue development and resolution related to dental scaling.Methods: This study featured a crossover design in which 20 dental hygienists completed two study arms, each consisting of four 2-minute scaling intervals separated by 30-second breaks, followed by 30 minutes of monitored rest.One study arm was completed using an adaptive silicone-over-steel curette, the other tested a rigid stainless-steel curette.The order of instrument use was randomized.Surface electromyography (sEMG) recorded muscle activity continuously in 4 muscles (abductor pollicis brevis, first dorsal interosseous, flexor pollicis longus, and extensor digitorum communis) through active intervals and rest periods.Linear mixed-effects models were used to test the primary sEMG outcome, with Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc comparisons.Recovery time was compared by Wilcoxon signed-rank test; Significance was set at p＜0.05.Results: Over the course of scaling, muscle activity increased significantly more with the rigid curette vs. the adaptive (p＜0.0001;η 2 =0.46).Each 30-second break achieved 24∼28% recovery towards baseline levels of muscle activity with the rigid curette vs. 39∼44% with the adaptive curette.By the end of the 30-minute monitored recovery period, muscle activity remained 13.9% above baseline for the rigid curette vs. 4.6% for the adaptive.The amount of time needed to recover to baseline levels of muscle activity was significantly quicker for the adaptive curette (155 seconds) vs. the rigid (295 seconds) (p=0.0003,r=0.61).Conclusion: Thirty-second breaks are inadequate for full neuromuscular recovery even after only 2 minutes of scaling.As the typical prophylaxis appointment lasts 30∼60 minutes, additional studies are needed to develop effective rest protocols to support neuromuscular recovery in healthy hygienists, and also in those with MSDs.An ergonomic adaptive handle design can reduce and support quicker recovery from muscle fatigue.Instrument selection is an important variable in maintaining a clinician's neuromuscular health and clinical performance.

Abstract This study examines the effectiveness of structured AI-supported learning in English vocabulary acquisition among undergraduate learners. A quasi-experimental design involved two intact B.A. Part-I student divisions at Shri Vijaysinha Yadav College, Peth Vadgaon. Both groups received instruction covering 100 target vocabulary items in four areas. The Experimental Group received teacher-guided support through an AI-Supported Vocabulary Learning Cycle using NotebookLM and ChatGPT for learning, practice, feedback, and revision. Both groups subsequently completed the same 100 item vocabulary post-test. Independent samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Cohen’s d were used. The Experimental Group achieved a significantly higher overall mean score (75.53) than the Control Group (66.95), t(70) = 6.39, p < .001, d = 1.51. All four categories showed significant differences, strongest for phrasal verbs. Gender showed no significant difference, whereas previous AI exposure and regular smartphone use were associated with higher achievement among Experimental Group learners. The findings suggest that AI can contribute to vocabulary learning when carefully and purposefully integrated with teacher-led classroom instruction and curriculum objectives. AI extends practice, feedback, revision, and application. Overall findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the intact-group design and absence of delayed assessment.

documents.abstract: This article analyses the effectiveness and perception of occupational safety and health (OSH) training using virtual reality (VR) compared to traditional methods. The aim of the study was to verify the effectiveness of VR training compared to traditional methods (Research No. 1) and to analyse the impressions of participants with different experiences with VR in the training system (Research No. 2). Research No. 1, conducted on students in the fields of construction and occupational health and safety, compared test results after traditional training (in person / online training) and VR (the “VR training at work at height” application). Research No. 2 included active construction workers, analysing their opinions on the usefulness, engagement, and impact of VR training on hazard knowledge, using questionnaires and participant observation. Research No. 1’s results showed a significant improvement in test scores after VRtraining (an average increase of 22%), suggesting a higher effectiveness of this method. In Research No. 2, participants rated highly the usefulness of VR in health and safety training, comfort with VR devices, and their own participation. The results of the study confirm the effectiveness of VR training in occupational safety and health, increasing the effectiveness and participation of participants. Immersion, visualisation, and simulation of harsh working conditions are key advantages of this technology. The VR training system combines the experience of virtual reality with learning theory, simulating emergency response procedures and procedures for the use of personal protective equipment.

Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of a large language model (LLM)-based intelligent adaptive teaching program in improving adverse event risk perception among newly employed nurses. Methods A prospective quasi-experimental study was conducted among 134 newly employed nurses recruited between July 2023 and July 2025 from a campus of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Zhejiang Province, China. Participants received training using an LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program. The Nurses' Risk Perception of Adverse Events Scale (NRPAES), the incidence of nursing adverse events, and training satisfaction were assessed before the intervention and 3 months after training. Differences in these outcomes before and after the intervention were analyzed. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 26.0, with the chi-square test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test used as appropriate. Results Following the LLM-based intelligent adaptive training, the adverse event risk perception score among newly employed nurses increased significantly from 14.95 (11.60, 17.29) before training to 16.22 (12.76, 19.00) after training ( Z = −3.527, P < 0.001). The overall incidence of nursing adverse events decreased significantly from 36 events (1.01‰) before training to 28 events (0.58‰) after training ( χ 2 = 5.060, P = 0.024). Visualization using a Sankey diagram further demonstrated an overall reduction in adverse events after the intervention. In addition, more than 90% of newly employed nurses reported satisfaction with each item of the satisfaction questionnaire for the LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program. Conclusion The LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program provides practical support for the individualized delivery of clinical risk perception training for newly employed nurses. The program may improve nurses' ability to perceive adverse event risks. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the integration of LLM-based tools into the design and delivery of nursing education programs.

Job satisfaction is widely recognised as a critical determinant of employee performance, organisational productivity, and long-term institutional effectiveness across diverse economic sectors. This paper examines the relationship between job satisfaction and employee performance through a comparative lens that considers both developed and developing country contexts. Drawing on a systematic literature review of empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025, the study synthesises evidence from a broad range of industries, including education, telecommunications, banking and financial services, information technology, automotive, healthcare, retail, construction, agriculture, logistics, energy, public administration, and manufacturing.The findings reveal a consistently positive and statistically significant association between job satisfaction and employee performance, either directly or through mediating mechanisms such as work engagement, organisational commitment, and motivation. Across sectors, job satisfaction is shaped by a combination of structural and motivational factors, including working conditions, training and development, leadership quality, compensation, career advancement opportunities, organisational support, and job design. Employees who report higher satisfaction levels tend to demonstrate stronger commitment, greater discretionary effort, higher productivity, and improved service quality.

This study explores how English as a Foreign Language (EFL) junior high school students engage with teacher written corrective feedback (WCF) and what their revision outcomes are. Studies of teacher WCF at the junior high school level in Indonesia remain limited, and few connect students’ engagement with the actual results of their revisions. This qualitative case study involved six eighth-grade students at a state junior high school in Karawang, West Java, selected purposively to represent low, medium, and high writing proficiency. Data came from semi-structured interviews and document analysis of the students’ first and second recount-text drafts. The findings show that all six students engaged cognitively, behaviorally, and affectively, but the depth of their engagement varied with proficiency. Behavioral engagement was the most dominant dimension because every student produced a revised draft; cognitive engagement was strong at the noticing stage yet uneven at the metacognitive level; and affective responses generally moved from negative to positive. Most revisions were successful, especially those responding to metalinguistic and direct feedback, while the few unsuccessful and misunderstood outcomes involved grammar and marks that only located errors. Teachers are therefore encouraged to introduce feedback codes before revision and to guide lower-proficiency students while they revise.

In hospital workflows, electronic health records (EHRs) are often noisy, and may not contain the evidence needed to confirm events or measurements referenced in a clinical query. Even when database retrieval succeeds, clinical agents can overlook such discrepancies and return plausible but unsupported answers. We introduce EHR-RobustGym, a scalable and interactive environment for evaluating and training robust clinical agents grounded in noisy EHRs. Built on MIMIC-IV hospital records (365K patients, 31 tables, and over 500M records), EHR-RobustGym comprises 5,486 Clean-Noise pairs spanning six clinical intents and both patient-level and population-level queries. The pairs test robustness to Record-level, Value-level, and Query-level noise, while interactive SQL/Python execution and outcome verification support trajectory collection and training. Evaluating multiple LLMs reveals substantial robustness gaps: average task success across proprietary and large-scale open-weight models drops from 62.2% on Clean questions to 37.9% on Noise questions. At k=4, pass^k consistency falls below 50% for most evaluated models, exposing instability in clinical task completion. Supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in EHR-RobustGym improve performance, with gains generalizing to five external EHR benchmarks. Together, these results position EHR-RobustGym as a testbed for evaluating and improving the evidence-grounded robustness of clinical agents.

documents.abstract: El nuevo Código Ético y Deontológico de la Enfermera Española surge en un momento clave para la profesión, al actualizar un marco que llevaba más de tres décadas sin revisar, al afrontar desafíos en la práctica, investigación y el uso de nuevas tecnologías. El código reconoce la madurez científica alcanzada por la enfermería y establece la investigación como un deber ético esencial para avanzar en nuestra disciplina y mejorar la calidad del cuidado. También incorpora competencias digitales e inteligencia artificial, recordando nuestra responsabilidad profesional en su aplicación. Este Código actualiza valores, amplía compromisos y ofrece un marco ético sólido para una enfermería que reconoce en la investigación el camino para mejorar la calidad de los cuidados y reforzar su impacto en la sociedad. ABSTRACT The new Code of Ethics and Deontology of the Spanish Nurse emerges at a pivotal moment for the profession, updating a framework that had remained unrevised for more than three decades while addressing contemporary challenges in practice, research, and the use of new technologies. The Code acknowledges the scientific maturity attained by nursing and establishes research as an essential ethical duty to advance the discipline and improve the quality of care. It also incorporates digital competencies and artificial intelligence, underscoring our professional responsibility in their implementation. This Code updates core values, expands professional commitments, and provides a robust ethical framework for a nursing discipline that recognizes research as the cornerstone for enhancing quality of care and strengthening its societal impact.

Background: The rapid rise of competitive esports has sparked concerns over the physical health of elite players. Prolonged sedentary behaviour, repetitive movements, and poor ergonomic practices may predispose these athletes to injuries, musculoskeletal pain, and unfavourable body composition. Materials and methods: A systematic review following PRISMA guidelines was conducted by searching Pub-Med, Scopus, EBSCOhost, and Web of Science for cross-sectional studies on physical activity (PA), body composition, physical fitness, and musculoskeletal health in elite esports players. Data from 22 peer-reviewed studies involving 5,035 participants aged 16 to 35 were synthesized. Results: Findings consistently show that esports players engage in lower levels of PA than recommended, with many recordings of daily step count and moderate-to-vigorous activity below normative guidelines. Although some maintain a normal body mass index (BMI), a significant subset exhibit elevated BMI and fat mass percentage, suggesting a risk for overweight and obesity-related conditions. Additionally, high rates of musculoskeletal complaints—including neck, back, wrist, and shoulder pain—are reported, with poor posture and reduced trunk muscle thickness evident in several studies. Conclusions: These results underscore the need for tailored health promotion strategies to enhance PA, optimize body composition, and reduce injury risk among esports athletes.

Capturing meaningful everyday moments is challenging as they often occur when users are cognitively absorbed or physically occupied. While always-on recording reduces “misses,” it introduces severe privacy concerns and data triage fatigue. We present EmbodiedRecall, a ring-to-glasses system that operationalizes a proactive capture paradigm. By continuously analyzing fine-grained hand dynamics via dual IMU-equipped rings, the system recognizes compositional motion primitives and utilizes a multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) to infer capture intent within hand-anchorable embodied moments. To balance agency with automation, EmbodiedRecall delivers subtle haptic or visual prompts, allowing users to “confirm-to-commit” short video clips from a privacy-preserving rolling buffer. A controlled lab study ( N = 20) validated our multi-stage pipeline, showing that our model significantly outperforms deep learning baselines with 75.35% accuracy. A 6-day active-session deployment ( N = 13) demonstrated that the system correctly aligns with user intent (46.5% confirmation rate) while surfacing serendipitous, emotionally resonant “micro-moments” users would not have captured manually. We discuss design implications for predictive wearables that enhance socio-emotional preservation while maintaining user agency.

Building fires and industrial thermal disasters rank among the most devastating hazards confronting modern societies, causing thousands of fatalities, billions of dollars in economic losses, and lasting environmental damage each year. The increasing complexity of built environments—including high-rise structures, underground facilities, and chemical processing plants—demands a commensurate advancement in emergency rescue technologies. This review provides a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art technologies employed in the detection, suppression, and rescue operations associated with building fires and industrial thermal disasters. Key domains covered include early fire detection systems integrating the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning; advanced fire suppression technologies such as water mist, gaseous agents, and high-expansion foam; autonomous and semi-autonomous rescue robotics; unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with thermal imaging; Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital twins for emergency planning and evacuation simulation; personal protective equipment (PPE) advancements including biometric wearables; and communication and situational-awareness systems. Special attention is given to industrial thermal hazards, including petrochemical fires, hazardous material incidents, BLEVE events, and dust explosions. The paper concludes with a critical synthesis of current research gaps and recommendations for future work, emphasizing integrated, data-driven, and human-centered approaches to emergency rescue.

Educational Robots are programmable robotic systems designed or adapted for teaching, learning, training, experimentation, and educational interaction. They can provide learners with opportunities to explore concepts through physical interaction, programming, problem-solving, experimentation, and project-based activities. Robotics brings together multiple areas of knowledge, including Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Electronics, and Design. In education, robots can therefore function not only as technological tools but also as platforms through which students develop computational thinking, creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. Educational robots may range from simple programmable devices used by young learners to sophisticated humanoid or autonomous robots used in higher education and research. Their educational role depends on the learner's age, curriculum, learning objectives, available infrastructure, and level of technological complexity. An Educational Robot is a robotic system used for educational purposes to support teaching, learning, experimentation, or skill development.A simplified learning process is: Learning Objective → Robot Activity → Student Interaction → Experimentation → Feedback → Learning The robot becomes a medium through which students can explore concepts and develop practical skills. The major objectives include: Making learning interactive Developing problem-solving skills Encouraging computational thinking Supporting programming education Promoting STEM learning Encouraging creativity Developing collaboration skills Connecting theory with practical experience Increasing learner engagement The objective is not simply to introduce robots into classrooms but to use robotics meaningfully to achieve educational outcomes. Robotics combines physical hardware with software and programming. A basic robotic learning system can be represented as: Input → Processing → Decision → Action → Feedback For example: Sensor Input → Program Logic → Motor Control → Robot Movement → Environmental Feedback Students can observe how computational instructions produce physical outcomes.

Emotion classification in music is a central problem in affective computing with critical applications in music therapy, personalized media, and emotionally adaptive systems. This study proposes a novel multi-modal stacking ensemble framework for multi-label music emotion recognition using the Emotify dataset. The proposed architecture integrates acoustic features, listener metadata (age, gender, mood), and genre information to capture both perceptual and contextual determinants of emotional response. Six modeling phases were evaluated using Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), XGBoost, and ensemble learning strategies. The final Stacking Ensemble, combining Random Forest, MLP, and XGBoost through a logistic regression meta-classifier, achieved a subset accuracy of 0.41, Hamming loss of 0.25, and macro-averaged F1 score of 0.67, outperforming all individual models as well as recent state-of-the-art approaches evaluated on the same Emotify dataset. Compared with existing CNN-LSTM and LLM-based methods, which report macro-F1 values below 0.51 or rely on shortsegment evaluation, the proposed framework delivers substantially higher performance on full-length music clips with strict multi-label evaluation. The results demonstrate that stacked ensemble learning combined with multi-modal feature fusion provides a robust and generalizable solution for modeling complex emotional landscapes in music, enabling accurate emotionaware music therapy systems, adaptive media platforms, and personalized music recommendation engines.

Abstract India’s digital transformation is creating a growing need for intelligent systems that can operate reliably across diverse sectors and linguistic settings. This paper presents a conceptual review of the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI), mathematics, and India’s digital development. The discussion focuses on agriculture, education, banking and financial services, legal services, transportation, digital commerce, and industry. Particular attention is given to the mathematical ideas that underpin AI: linear algebra for representing data and parameters; probability and statistics for uncertainty and inference; calculus for gradient-based learning; and optimization for selecting model parameters and making decisions. Mathematical modelling is further considered as a bridge between real-world systems and data-driven methods. The paper also examines responsible and inclusive AI, emphasizing reliability, privacy, fairness, transparency, security, accountability, and human oversight. India’s national AI strategy and the India’s AI Mission provide a policy context for these developments, while recent international assessment work highlights the importance of human-centred and ethical deployment. The paper argues that India’s long-term AI capacity should be developed through a coordinated emphasis on computing infrastructure, high-quality data, mathematical education, interdisciplinary research, multilingual technologies, and responsible governance.

This study investigated English-major students’ perceptions of AI-assisted tools in IELTS Writing Task 2 practice at Thanh Do University, Vietnam. The study aimed to explore how students perceived the usefulness and challenges of using AI-assisted writing technologies during IELTS-oriented writing activities. A qualitative research design was employed, involving semi-structured interviews with 15 third-year English-major students enrolled in the Integrated English 2 course during the second semester of the 2025 academic year. The participants had experience using AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, and Gemini to support IELTS Writing Task 2 practice. Interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that students generally perceived AI-assisted writing tools positively due to their usefulness in idea generation, essay organization, grammar correction, vocabulary enhancement, and self-study support. Participants also believed that AI technologies improved writing confidence and encouraged learner autonomy. However, concerns regarding overreliance on AI-generated content, reduced independent thinking, and the reliability of AI-generated feedback were also identified. The study highlights the potential of AI-assisted writing technologies as supplementary learning resources in IELTS-oriented writing instruction while emphasizing the importance of responsible and balanced AI integration in higher education contexts.

documents.abstract: While large language models have achieved remarkable success in isolated code generation, authentic software engineering requires sustained reasoning, complex state management, and continuous cross-domain abstraction. However, current evaluations of skill evolution in autonomous agents suffer from a critical identifiability problem: they structurally confound genuine capability abstraction with rote solution leakage (i.e., copying highly similar code from historical training data). To resolve this, we introduce EngramBench, a rigorous, capability-grounded benchmark governed by the strict axiom of capability overlap without solution overlap. Comprising 30 diverse learning tasks and 13 unseen transfer tasks, EngramBench challenges agents to navigate interactive, multi-hour development cycles driven by LLM-simulated users. Our extensive evaluation across 48 multi-hour execution trajectories -- corroborated by human-expert validation -- reveals a profound insight into procedural memory. We demonstrate that static skill banks do not magically bypass the "last mile" of exact code implementation, which remains bottlenecked by the base model's inherent reasoning limits. However, they serve as an indispensable execution compass. By navigating agents away from catastrophic, token-heavy trial-and-error, genuine capability abstraction slashes redundant context bloat and reduces overall coding time by over 55%. Ultimately, EngramBench shifts the evaluation paradigm from trivial pattern matching to the verifiable measurement of deep, cross-domain capability transfer.

Few-step autoregressive video generation enables efficient streaming synthesis, but errors introduced in early temporal blocks are reused as context and can propagate through subsequent rollouts, leading to detail degradation, structural drift, and unstable motion. Existing distribution matching distillation (DMD) primarily aligns student and teacher distributions in diffusion latent space, but provides no direct supervision over the perceptual quality of decoded videos. We introduce Radian, a representation-space adversarial distillation framework that complements on-policy DMD with real-data adversarial supervision in the feature space defined by a frozen visual foundation model (VFM). During training, Radian sparsely decodes frames from autoregressive student rollouts, extracts multi-level visual representations, and applies lightweight discriminator heads to distinguish generated outputs from real video frames. The DMD objective anchors the student to the pretrained teacher, while the representation-space adversarial objective supplies complementary perceptual and semantic gradients that promote high-quality modes. These additional components are discarded after training, leaving the generator architecture and inference-time denoising budget unchanged. Experiments on Wan2.1-1.3B cover four-step chunk-wise, one-step frame-wise, and minute-long autoregressive generation. Our method achieves a VBench Total of 0.8444 and a VideoAlign Total of 0.8033 under four-step generation, and improves VBench-Long from 0.7805 to 0.8041 over Rolling Forcing while using fewer denoising steps. Controlled comparisons across image, video, and diffusion representations further indicate that the choice of representation spaces induces distinct adversarial signals, and external VFM gradients complement DMD more effectively than adversarial supervision derived from diffusion-internal features.

documents.abstract: Pronunciation is one of the most difficult areas of second language acquisition and more especially for EFL learners. Typical classroom settings can be difficult to provide individual pronunciation feedback and corrective feedback. The recent developments of Artificial Intelligence (AI) especially language learning through AI speech recognition have revolutionized the way language is learned, providing instant, personalized and data-driven pronunciation feedback. This paper proposes to examine how well AI speech recognition technology can improve the pronunciation skills of learners. The study is based on previous research, theories on second language acquisition, and current advances in education technology to explore the role of AI applications in facilitating pronunciation accuracy, learner autonomy, motivation, and confidence. The paper proposes that in the field of pronunciation learning, continuously assessing and providing immediate corrective feedback on students' pronunciation through AI-based speech recognition technology can generate adaptive learning experiences and effectively enhance pronunciation learning outcomes. However, the potential for educating with them is only realized if a number of issues are tackled, including technology, accent bias, privacy and accessibility. The results indicate that the use of AI pronunciation tools in language teaching could enhance the learning atmosphere and be effective when combined with a classical language teaching method.

This conference paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-based learning environments can enhance student engagement in higher education. The study focuses on the integration of learning analytics, recommendation systems, intelligent tutoring, adaptive feedback, and interactive programming tasks to support behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social engagement. The proposed model links learner profiling, real-time analytics, personalization, feedback, and pedagogical design into a unified engagement-oriented learning environment. A model-based experimental framework is presented with sample indicators and illustrative results. The findings suggest that AI-supported adaptive learning environments may increase student participation, improve persistence in programming tasks, strengthen self-regulated learning, and support the development of programming competence. The paper also discusses implementation challenges, including data privacy, teacher readiness, infrastructure, and the need for human-centered AI design. Keywords: artificial intelligence, student engagement, AI-based learning environment, learning analytics, adaptive feedback, personalized learning

documents.abstract: Persistent personal AI agents may change the relationship between an individual's attention and productive capacity. This paper defines Agentomaly as a proposed transition in which individuals can affordably sustain adaptive, concurrent delegated work that previously required more direct attention or organizational support. Delegation and automation are not new. The hypothesis concerns a change in their accessibility, flexibility, persistence, and coordination cost at the level of the individual principal. The paper distinguishes three questions: whether agents expand individual productive capacity; whether their interactions become a substantial operational layer of the economy; and whether the resulting systems preserve meaningful human authority. These outcomes need not coincide. A closed platform could deliver large productivity gains while concentrating control and making exit difficult. The proposed analytical unit is the principal-agent relationship. Its performance should be evaluated through quality-adjusted completed outcomes, principal attention, total human labor, elapsed time, resource cost, and externalities. More agent activity is not evidence of more economic value. The paper also develops the Principal Concentration Problem: many agent identities may represent one controlling organization rather than independent market participants. A governance framework addresses bounded mandates, audit, continuity, portability, and human re-entry. These are design commitments to assess separately from productivity, not assumed consequences of technical capability. A research agenda proposes comparisons with manual work, AI-assisted work, conventional automation, and human delegation. The 2030 horizon is a scenario boundary, not a forecast. The contribution is an integrated framework for testing when persistent delegation expands individual agency, how its benefits and costs are distributed, and whether its expansion remains subject to effective human control.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This chapter advances a decolonial framework for the epistemic stakes of AI-augmented thinking pedagogy in global higher education. Without deliberate intervention, the integration of generative AI into design thinking risks operationalising at a computational scale the colonial knowledge hierarchies long carried in less visible form by design thinking as a travelling pedagogy of Anglo-American provenance. The argument synthesises three theoretical resources. Fricker&s;s account of testimonial and hermeneutical injustice, extended through Dotson&s;s analysis of contributory injustice, supplies the framework&s;s analytic architecture. Santos&s;s diagnosis of abyssal thinking locates these harms within the longer history of epistemic colonialism, while Mignolo&s;s colonial matrix of power and political horizon of pluriversality orient the analysis toward pedagogical reconstruction rather than incremental adjustment. From this synthesis the chapter develops a three-dimensional framework identifying testimonial, hermeneutical, and contributory justice as conditions for responsible AI integration. A worked example from an undergraduate Gulf university course, in which students engage Syrian refugee educational experiences through refugee-authored sources rather than direct fieldwork, illustrates the framework alongside its ethical and institutional conditions. The chapter recasts AI ethics as a question of pedagogical formation for which educators and institutions, not technical systems, bear principal responsibility.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: As artificial intelligence reshapes the epistemic foundations of teaching, educators face unprecedented decisions about which knowledge practices to preserve, delegate or transform. This study introduces ‘epistemic negotiation’ as a conceptual lens to examine how educators actively deliberate about AI’s boundaries in knowledge work rather than passively accepting or rejecting technology. Moving beyond adoption-focused research, the study presents a typological analysis of AI-mediated Knowledge Management (KM) amongst 454 Indian educators. Using exploratory factor analysis and k-means clustering, four distinct profiles were identified: Disengaged, Instrumental Users, Process-Focused and High-fidelity Users, differentiated by epistemic orientations rather than technical competence. The findings reposition AI integration as primarily a knowledge management challenge. Theoretically, the study advances KM frameworks for analysing educational technology. Practically, the findings demonstrate that professional development must cultivate epistemic reflexivity and KM competencies over technical skills. For policy, the typology challenges uniform mandates, advocating differentiated support structures that honour diverse knowledge practices whilst establishing ethical parameters.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Erdőfigyelő (Hungarian for “forest watcher”; forest.equora.institute) is a public web system that links citizen reports on forests and water, open satellite change alerts, and forest-compartment records from the Hungarian National Forest Stand Database (NÉBIH) on a single map. This white paper describes the architecture, the data sources and the processing methods — a forest mask, cell-based patch delineation, the per-patch daily alerted area, pixel-level intersection with Natura 2000 sites and a single-date 2021 tree-cover flag from ESA WorldCover — as well as report moderation and privacy-by-design measures. First results as of 30 September 2026: between 1 January and 21 September 2026, 3,734 DIST-ALERT patches of at least 3 ha were recorded within the forest mask (total patch area 30,994.5 ha). Of the tree cover loss in Hungary between 2001 and 2017 (approx. 182 kha), 81.7% falls on cells classified as tree cover in ESA WorldCover 2021. In the Börzsöny sample area, 87.4% of the 582.8 ha alerted in the third quarter of 2026 lies within Natura 2000 sites. Pixel-level intermediate results are published, so that the area figures can be recomputed independently. The paper documents the limitations, the corrections made after human testing and three rounds of AI-assisted audits (ChatGPT-6 Astra) under the EQUORA Trilith Method™, with a dated correction log, and a research agenda led by a pre-specified, stratified national validation with drone-based field verification (Olofsson et al. 2014; Stehman 2014). Version 1.1 adds the third audit round, annual areas by pixel year for the 2024–2025 patches, both named measures for the sample boundary, explicit accuracy estimators and a Research Card. Files: English version (erdofigyelo-white-paper-v1.1-en.pdf) and Hungarian version (erdofigyelo-white-paper-v1.1-hu.pdf).Open data (CC BY 4.0): forest.equora.institute/nyilt-adat Magyar összefoglaló. Az Erdőfigyelő nyilvános webes rendszer, amely egy térképen kapcsolja össze a lakossági erdő- és vízügyi bejelentéseket, a nyilvános műholdas változásjelzéseket és a NÉBIH erdőrészlet-adatait. A dokumentum a rendszer felépítését, módszertanát, első eredményeit, korlátait és kutatási tervét írja le; a magyar változat a második fájl.

documents.abstract: Uncovering new phenomena in nature requires experiments. For centuries, their design has been exclusively a human endeavor. Today, a new paradigm is emerging in which artificial intelligence and computational methods can design experiments themselves. Realizing this form of automated scientific discovery requires simulators that are sufficiently expressive to represent the diverse physical processes and couplings from which new experiments can be constructed. In this direction, we introduce \textsc{esQueranto}, a differentiable software that brings photon-number quantum optics and structured-light propagation into a common description, allowing the spatial evolution of light to directly influence non-classical quantum states and their interference. \textsc{esQueranto} is implemented in JAX, providing automatic differentiation and hardware-accelerated evaluation for optimization and automated search. We demonstrate the framework across a broad range of quantum-optical applications that exercise complementary aspects of its physical description. By combining quantum and structured-light physics within a single differentiable simulator, \textsc{esQueranto} takes an important step towards the dream of a foundational simulator in physics.

This article highlights the importance of the principles of medical ethics and deontology in the professional activities of healthcare workers. Particular attention is paid to humanism, respect, trust, professional responsibility, medical confidentiality, respect for patients’ rights, and informed consent in the relationship between healthcare workers and patients. The article also analyzes new deontological issues arising in modern medicine, including the use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence, protection of patient data, and compliance with professional ethical standards when using social media.The communicative competence of healthcare workers, the culture of teamwork, and the prevention of occupational stress are also considered important factors in ensuring the quality of medical care. Keywords: medical ethics, deontology, healthcare worker, patient, professional responsibility, medical confidentiality, informed consent, communication, patients’ rights

documents.abstract: Background and rationale Digital health technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly transforming healthcare delivery, health professional education, clinical decision-making, workforce development, and health-system organisation. The World Health Organization (WHO) recognises digital health as an important mechanism for strengthening health systems and improving access to equitable, efficient and high-quality healthcare (World Health Organization [WHO], 2025a), reflecting the continuing importance of digital health transformation globally (WHO, 2025b). AI has particular potential to influence clinical decision-making, service delivery, education and research. In nursing and midwifery, AI technologies have been applied across direct patient care, administration and management, and, to a lesser extent, education. A systematic review by O’Connor et al. (2023) identified 140 studies involving applications of AI to nursing and midwifery, with most applications directed towards clinical practice and patient care. However, the review also identified important limitations and risks, including poor-quality datasets and potential bias, privacy and trust concerns, the need for clinical interpretation of AI-generated results, and limited AI expertise among nurses and midwives. These findings demonstrate that implementation of AI is not solely a technological issue but also has professional, educational, ethical and governance implications. The rapid adoption of AI and other digital technologies creates opportunities to improve healthcare access, efficiency, clinical decision-making and patient outcomes, while simultaneously raising significant ethical, legal and social concerns. The WHO has emphasised that ethics and human rights should be central to the design, development, deployment and use of AI for health (WHO, 2021). Its guidance identifies principles including protecting human autonomy; promoting the public interest; ensuring transparency, explainability and intelligibility; fostering responsibility and accountability; and promoting AI that is responsive and sustainable. These principles highlight the importance of considering ethics throughout the lifecycle of health technologies rather than only after technologies have been implemented. Ethical considerations are especially important in nursing because nurses have sustained interactions with patients and families and frequently engage with health information systems, digital technologies and clinical decision-support tools at the point of care. The increasing incorporation of AI into nursing therefore raises questions concerning professional accountability, autonomy, informed consent, privacy and confidentiality, data security, algorithmic bias, transparency, equity, patient safety, trust and preservation of human-centred care (Badawy et al., 2025; Mohammed et al., 2025). Ethical issues are also emerging in nursing education as generative AI becomes increasingly accessible to students and educators. De Gagne et al. (2024) argue that the integration of AI into nursing education requires consideration of established ethical principles, including autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice and explicability. They emphasise the need for ethical principles to be incorporated into curricula and for appropriate guidance to support responsible AI use. Other nursing education literature has similarly identified potential benefits of AI and AI-enabled chatbots for personalised learning, simulation, accessibility and educator support, alongside concerns relating to privacy, confidentiality, bias and appropriate use (Srinivasan et al., 2024). Despite increasing recognition of these issues, the evidence relevant to nursing remains dispersed across different technologies, settings, populations and types of ethical consideration. Existing reviews demonstrate that ethical challenges associated with AI in nursing are substantial (Badawy et al., 2025; Mohammed et al., 2025), while broader reviews demonstrate considerable variation in how AI is being introduced and evaluated across nursing and midwifery practice (O’Connor et al., 2023). However, identifying ethical concerns alone does not establish what ethical frameworks, guidelines, principles or governance approaches are being used to guide the conceptualisation and application of these technologies, nor how such guidance is operationalised in nursing education and practice. There is therefore a need to systematically map primary research addressing the ethical conceptualisation and application of AI and digital health innovations within nursing. In particular, it is important to identify the ethical guidelines, frameworks, principles and empirically derived recommendations reported in the literature; describe their underlying characteristics and intended applications; and examine the factors associated with their implementation or application in nursing education and practice. Such mapping can clarify the current evidence base, identify areas of convergence and inconsistency, reveal gaps between ethical principles and their practical implementation, and identify priorities for future nursing research, education, professional guidance and governance. Accordingly, this scoping review aims to map how AI and digital health innovations are conceptualised and applied ethically in nursing practice and education. A scoping review is appropriate because the purpose is to examine the breadth and characteristics of the available evidence, identify the ethical frameworks and principles represented across heterogeneous primary studies, and explore factors associated with their application rather than determine the effectiveness of a single intervention. Aim: The overall aim of this scoping review is to map how artificial intelligence and digital health innovations are conceptualised and applied ethically in nursing practice and education. The review will additionally map, where reported: • the characteristics and underlying ethical principles of identified guidelines, frameworks or recommendations; • the types of AI and digital health technologies to which ethical considerations are applied; • the nursing settings and populations in which these considerations arise; • the intended or actual applications of identified ethical guidance in nursing education and clinical practice; and • barriers, facilitators and other contextual considerations associated with ethical implementation and use. documents.abstract: Fairness is one of the fundamental ethical principles governing the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education. AI systems increasingly influence learning recommendations, assessment, student support, admissions, academic advising, and institutional decision-making. Because these systems can affect educational opportunities, fairness must be considered throughout their design, development, deployment, and evaluation. An AI system is not automatically fair simply because it uses mathematical or computational methods. If the data, assumptions, objectives, or decision processes contain bias, the resulting system may reproduce or amplify existing inequalities. A simplified framework is: Educational Data → AI Model → Prediction/Recommendation → Educational Decision → Student Outcome Fairness requires examining every stage of this process. Fairness in AI-based education refers to the principle that learners should be treated equitably and should not experience unjustified disadvantage because of characteristics unrelated to legitimate educational objectives.Fairness involves: Equal opportunity Non-discrimination Appropriate treatment Inclusive access Consistent evaluation Protection from unjustified bias Fairness does not always mean treating every learner identically. Different learners may require different forms of support to achieve equitable educational opportunities. The major objectives include: Reducing discriminatory outcomes Providing equitable educational opportunities Identifying and reducing algorithmic bias Supporting inclusive learning Ensuring equitable access to AI systems Protecting vulnerable learners Promoting trustworthy educational technologies Fairness should be considered throughout: Data Collection → Model Development → Testing → Deployment → Monitoring A system that is fair during development may produce unfair outcomes after deployment if the educational environment changes. AI systems learn from data. If historical educational data contain unequal patterns, an AI system may reproduce them. For example: Historical Bias → Training Data → AI Model → Potentially Biased Prediction

documents.abstract: When Isaac Newton discovered the law of gravitation, he did so through an iterative process of analyzing observed data such as planetary patterns, finding the underlying mechanisms by describing patterns in mathematical equations, and refining his theory against the Moon's orbit, revealing the startling insight that the same force governs both falling apples and orbiting planets. Would it be possible for AI agents to make similar discoveries? To measure this ability, we introduce EurekaBench, a cross-domain benchmark that tests AI agents' ability to conduct long-horizon experiments and discover mechanisms that explain observations. We evaluate these mechanisms by the scientific insights that can be derived from them. EurekaBench contains an expert-verified set of 26 long-horizon tasks across neuroscience, computer science, chemistry, astrophysics, geophysics, and plasma physics, with a total of 306 scientific insights that the discovered mechanisms are expected to support. Our evaluation framework tests three axes of scientific discovery: agents' ability to follow known scientific constraints, the predictive accuracy of the discovered mechanisms, and whether these mechanisms yield scientific insights or inform future research. Our results show that current AI agents often overly fixate on predictive accuracy optimization, surpassing human scientists, while falling substantially short in deriving scientific insights.

Ergonomics is a scientific discipline that aims to adapt working conditions to individuals' capabilities and limitations in order to improve safety, well-being, and job performance. In the educational context, its application is essential for protecting teachers' occupational health, as they are exposed to various ergonomic risk factors throughout their workday. The objective of this study was to evaluate the ergonomic conditions of teachers' workstations in an educational institution using the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) method. A quantitative, descriptive, and cross-sectional approach was employed, analyzing the postures adopted during the main teaching activities. The findings revealed that prolonged writing on the blackboard obtained a RULA score of 7, indicating a very high-risk level that requires immediate intervention. Likewise, prolonged use of technological devices reached a score of 6, while reviewing academic tasks and prolonged standing each obtained scores of 5, classifying these activities as high risk. It is concluded that preventive and corrective ergonomic measures should be implemented to reduce the identified risks and prevent the development of musculoskeletal disorders among teaching staff.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) marks a shift from reactive educational technologies towards systems capable of autonomous multi-step planning, tool orchestration, and adaptive decision-making. As these systems contribute to structuring study pathways, generating feedback, and monitoring learner progression, elements of cognitive and metacognitive regulation become distributed between learners and AI agents. However, existing evaluation approaches in educational technology remain largely focused on usability, performance, and satisfaction, and are therefore insufficient to capture these dynamic and distributed forms of agency. This paper proposes the Multi-Layer Evaluation Model for Agentic AI (MLE-A), a conceptual framework for assessing the educational impact of agentic systems across five interacting dimensions: cognitive, metacognitive, affective, behavioural, and system-level governance. The model provides a structured basis for analysing human–AI collaboration and supporting future empirical evaluation.

documents.abstract: Background Office workers accumulate most of their waking h in sedentary behavior, yet scalable personalized occupational-health advice remains limited, and the quality of large language model (LLM)-based tools in this domain has not been rigorously examined. Objective This study evaluated whether a domain-specialized chatbot system for providing health advice on sedentary behavior, integrating retrieval augmentation, a curated corpus, and safety guardrails, performs better than a general-purpose LLM and static educational materials. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was used. In the blinded expert evaluation, nine raters independently rated 60 responses across five quality dimensions. In the user survey, 654 eligible Chinese office workers interacted with the specialized chatbot and completed six perception scales (two adapted from established technology-acceptance frameworks and four developed for this study) plus open-ended feedback. Results Inter-rater reliability was good for the composite score; in a case-level safety screen, no response from the specialized chatbot or the standard materials was flagged as potentially unsafe, whereas two Doubao responses were flagged by two or more raters. The specialized chatbot achieved the highest composite rating, followed by Doubao and standard materials. In a linear mixed-effects model and crossed random intercepts for rater and question, all Holm-adjusted pairwise contrasts were significant. Advantages of the specialized chatbot over Doubao were most pronounced on safety in symptom-management and special-population items. Among users, perceived ease of use was highest, whereas perceived safety and intention to use were rated comparatively lower. Frequent prior AI-chatbot use was associated with higher ratings on all six scales; after covariate adjustment the association persisted for five of the six scales but was attenuated and no longer significant for perceived safety. Conclusion The specialized chatbot system received expert-rated accuracy and safety scores that did not differ significantly from standard educational materials, but exceeded standard materials on usefulness, comprehensibility, and completeness, and outperformed the general-purpose LLM on accuracy, safety, completeness, and the overall composite score. These findings concern response quality and immediate user perceptions, not behavioral or clinical outcomes. Nonetheless, users remained cautious about safety and intention to use after this brief exposure.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Care-plan formulation is among the most cognitively demanding competencies that pre-registration nursing students must master, and errors made at this formative stage may persist into qualified practice. Two contemporary developments converge on this competency: the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) capable of suggesting nursing diagnoses and interventions, and the normalization of the telemedicine practicum as a clinical learning environment. No prior synthesis has examined their intersection. The aim of this study is to identify, appraise, and synthesize the evidence on the effect of AI-driven CDSS on the accuracy of nursing students’ care-plan formulation within telemedicine practicum settings. The review is designed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and conducted with reference to the Cochrane Handbook and the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis. Eight databases and grey-literature sources searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies published between 2015 and 2026. Screening, extraction, and appraisal were performed in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed with design-appropriate instruments (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, JBI checklists, MMAT), and certainty was rated using GRADE. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, and a structured narrative synthesis following SWiM guidance was undertaken. The evidence converges on a conditional benefit. Structured, taxonomy-aligned decision support raised students’ diagnostic and care-plan accuracy relative to unsupported practice, with the inference model, the supervision arrangement, and learner characteristics acting as decisive moderators. Generative large language models produced substantial gains in rated plan quality but exhibited a characteristic failure mode of fluent yet taxonomy-discordant output, creating conditions in which automation bias is most hazardous. The telemedicine setting amplified both the potential benefit and the risk of uncritical reliance. The study concludes that an AI-driven CDSS functions as a conditional cognitive scaffold rather than an unconditional accelerator of accuracy. Its educational value in the telemedicine practicum is realized only where outputs are aligned with recognized nursing taxonomies, system reasoning is transparent, and use is embedded within supervised, deliberate practice that preserves the student as the accountable clinical reasoner. Recommendations are made for nursing education, policy, and future primary research.

Objectives: This study aimed to compare the performance of DeepSeek-V3, ChatGPT 4.0, ChatGPT 4.5, Gemini Advanced 2.0, and Grok in answering single-correct answer multiple-choice (SCQ), multiple-correct answer multiple-choice (MCQ), binary (true/false) (BQ), and open-ended questions (OEQ) based on the European Society of Endodontology (ESE) position statements.Materials and Methods: A total of 70 questions (24 SCQ/MCQ, 29 BQ, and 17 OEQ) were posed to five LLMs. Responses were scored on a 0–10 scale for comprehensiveness, scientific accuracy, clarity, and relevance. SCQ, MCQ, and BQ formats were additionally evaluated for correctness (1 = correct, 0 = incorrect). Data were analyzed using Pearson’s chi-square test and the Kruskal-Wallis H test (p < 0.05).Results: In the SCQ/MCQ format, Gemini Advanced 2.0 scored significantly higher than Grok. In the BQ format, ChatGPT 4.5 and Gemini Advanced 2.0 achieved significantly higher scores than ChatGPT 4.0 and Grok. In the OEQ format, ChatGPT 4.5 obtained significantly higher scores than Grok (p < 0.05). Accuracy rates were 67.9% for ChatGPT 4.5, 66.0% for Gemini Advanced 2.0, 58.5% for DeepSeek-V3, 52.8% for ChatGPT 4.0, and 49.1% for Grok (p > 0.05). In all models, scientific accuracy scores were significantly lower than relevance scores (p < 0.05).Conclusions: ChatGPT 4.5 and Gemini Advanced 2.0 demonstrated stronger performance than the other models, whereas Grok showed lower response-content performance. However, since LLMs may appear convincing even when generating incorrect clinical information, they should be used only as supplementary tools in endodontic education and preliminary information retrieval. Clinically relevant outputs should be verified by an endodontist or an appropriately qualified clinician.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The well-being of educators is a cornerstone of high-quality education. However, teachers in the expanding global private school sector face significant workplace stressors. Increasing competition and pressure to perform can negatively impact both student achievement and school climate by increasing workloads and burnout. This study examines the relationship between psychosocial risks and job satisfaction among private school teachers in Türkiye, a country with a globally competitive education environment. This research focused on private school teachers working in Erzurum province. Data were collected using Google forms after obtaining ethics committee approval. Using a cross-sectional design, 203 teachers were surveyed using the Copenhagen Psychosocial Risk Questionnaire (COPSOQ-TR) and Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ). The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 25 software, employing descriptive statistics, normality (Shapiro-Wilk) and homogeneity of variance (Levene) tests, t-tests, the Mann-Whitney U test, ANOVA, the Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal-Wallis test, and Spearman’s correlation analysis. Statistical analysis revealed a strong and significant negative correlation between general psychosocial risk and job satisfaction (r = -.803, p < .001). In particular, it was found that organizational factors such as weak leadership, lack of fairness, and insufficient recognition had a greater negative impact on satisfaction than workload demands. The importance of a supportive and fair organizational environment has been emphasized. Additionally, a positive correlation was found between burnout and job satisfaction, suggesting the existence of a complex “commitment paradox” among highly dedicated teachers in the field. Demographic characteristics, such as gender, age, teaching experience, marital status, and whether teachers had received occupational health and safety (OHS) training, also significantly influenced the perception of specific risks, such as burnout and work-family conflict. These findings underscore the need for systematic interventions. Proactive risk management, leadership development focused on promoting fairness and support, and policies aimed at enhancing teachers’ resilience are vital. Protecting teachers’ well-being is not only a necessity from an occupational health perspective, but also a direct investment in maintaining the quality of education.

Modern ship operations use strict procedures and advanced automation, which may reduce seafarers’ experience in handling unexpected situations. This study aims to analyze the relationship between exception exposure deprivation and emergency readiness vulnerability among seafarers. A quantitative correlational method was conducted through a questionnaire survey involving 100 seafarers and maritime trainees in Banten, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression. The results indicate that limited exposure to abnormal situations is associated with lower emergency readiness among seafarers. This study highlights the importance of realistic emergency training and varied scenarios to improve maritime safety and human performance.

This study examines the role of the exchange rate as an interactive predictor in artificial intelligence (AI) models for financial distress prediction in Iraqi private banks. Earlier financial-distress studies have primarily emphasized bank-specific financial ratios or have treated macroeconomic variables as additive controls. The present study instead investigates whether exchange-rate conditions modify the relationship between bank-specific financial indicators and the probability of distress. The empirical analysis uses a panel of 170 bank-year observations for 10 Iraqi private banks listed on the Iraq Stock Exchange over the period 2008–2024. Logistic Regression is used as the conventional benchmark, while Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Artificial Neural Network models are used as machine-learning alternatives; Cox proportional hazards analysis is additionally used to examine interaction effects in a time-to-distress framework. The comparative results show that Random Forest achieved the highest reported classification performance, with an accuracy of 98.1%, sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 100%, F1-score of 92.3%, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.898. Interaction analysis indicates that the exchange rate significantly moderates the association between non-performing loans and financial distress and also modifies the effect of selected profitability indicators. Decision-tree rules further reveal exchange-rate thresholds that alter distress classification conditional on profitability and credit quality. Variable-importance analyses consistently place profitability, credit quality, and the exchange rate among the most influential predictors. These findings support an interaction-based interpretation of banking risk in which macroeconomic conditions change the informational value of bank-specific indicators rather than merely adding an independent source of risk. The study contributes to the financial-distress literature by integrating model comparison, interaction analysis, and interpretable

Generative artificial intelligence can contribute to the representations, alternatives and evaluations through which executive judgements are formed. Existing research already explains important aspects of hybrid cognition, reliance, managerial agency and accountability. This article develops a narrower process challenge: locally competent human and AI contributions can still culminate in an inadequately warranted organisational commitment when established operational assumptions, uncertainties or dependencies are lost or transformed before authorisation. It proposes qualification attrition as the process through which such epistemically consequential content is weakened across successive transformations, and a formation--authorisation gap as the resulting discrepancy between the grounds required for warranted commitment and those that remain accessible, intelligible and challengeable to the authorising role. Executive judgement governance is defined through four dimensions: boundary setting, interpretive challenge, reliance calibration, and authorisation with answerability. Four propositions connect transformation, qualification attrition and governance arrangements to epistemic risk, accountability risk and judgement quality. The contribution is an integrative process theory of how distributed judgement formation can fail as a composition even where individual contributions, local reliance decisions and formal accountability arrangements appear competent.

documents.abstract: This study, focusing on sustainable energy production and particularly the hydrogen (H 2 ) economy, presents an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) framework for accurately predicting H 2 production from sucrose photocatalysis catalyzed by LaFeO 3 (GLFO) and the H 2 concentration in syngas derived from biomass conversion. The research was conducted along two main directions: (i) deep learning (DL) architectures comprising nine specially designed recurrent neural network-based models and (ii) six conventional machine learning (ML) algorithms. For both H 2 production systems, the best-performing models were identified and further interpreted using explainable AI (XAI) based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Among all investigated algorithms, a hybrid One-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory–Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (1D-CNN–BiLSTM–BiGRU) model demonstrated the highest predictive performance. Using 10-fold cross-validation, the proposed model achieved outstanding accuracy, with an R 2 value of 0.9987 ± 0.0011 for photocatalytic H 2 production prediction and 0.9980 ± 0.0006 for syngas H 2 concentration prediction. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework as a precise, reliable, and practical methodological approach for modeling and optimizing complex thermochemical energy systems.

Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites offer high specific strength, high stiffness, and good corrosion resistance, which suits them to aerospace, automotive, marine, and wind energy structures. Their interlaminar fracture behaviour is harder to pin down, because delamination testing is slow and costly and the response shifts with loading mode. This study presents an explainable hybrid machine learning framework for interlaminar fracture toughness under Mode-I, Mode-II, and Mixed-Mode loading. A weighted ensemble pairs Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), a gradient boosting method, with the Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN), a pretrained transformer built for tabular data. A Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) tunes the CatBoost hyperparameters and the ensemble weight against specimen-grouped cross-validation. The work draws on the public D-STANDART experimental dataset and treats DCB, ELS, and MMB as three separate prediction problems for GIC, GIIC, and GC rather than pooling them into one model. Partitioning runs at specimen level, so no coupon supplies records to more than one subset, and feature selection uses training data alone. SHAP then measures how each input shifts predicted toughness in each mode. The framework reached R² of 0.9280 for DCB, 0.9870 for ELS, and 0.9627 for MMB, with RMSE of 5.1759, 1.5041, and 2.8809 and MAE of 1.6502, 0.5372, and 0.7000. Bringing a tabular foundation model into delamination analysis, and keeping the three loading modes apart, lets the framework report mode-specific feature behaviour instead of one averaged picture.

LLM agents often admit multiple high-quality solutions to the same task, differing in reasoning structure, tool-use pattern, or interaction trajectory. Yet existing notions of diversity in LLM post-training are mostly implicit, arising from general stochasticity and regularization mechanisms rather than explicitly targeting task-relevant behavioral variation. While such implicit diversity can be useful, it does not directly specify which forms of behavioral variation should be encouraged for a given task. In this work, we study explicit trajectory diversity in RL-based post-training for LLMs. Our key idea is to define diversity through user-specified, task-specific trajectory descriptors, which map each sampled trajectory to an interpretable behavioral representation, and then measure diversity as a set-level functional over the resulting descriptor matrix. Building on this formulation, we introduce Trajectory-guided Joint Policy Optimization(TJPO), a single-policy framework that optimizes explicit diversity over sampled trajectory groups, avoiding the need for population-based policy training, and instantiate it within group-based policy optimization through trajectory-level learning signals. This design makes the diversity objective both interpretable and controllable. Experiments on Sokoban and ALFWorld show that TJPO improves task-specific trajectory diversity while maintaining competitive task performance. Descriptor and trajectory analyses show that the learned variation follows the specified behavioral dimensions and includes distinct successful strategies. Extra experiment results suggest that explicitly shaping trajectory diversity can help LLM agents satisfy user requirements and remain effective when task conditions change.

This work outlines an experimental framework to examine how large language models (LLMs) construct and reproduce narratives about international movements of people, which includes migration and displacement.
